# `Q-19-4` — Brand Color Not Applied To Plot

> A brand color meant to recolor a hephaestus plot is not a hex color,
> so the plot keeps its own color for that slot.

## What this means

When a document declares a brand (`brand: _brand.yml`), Quarto
recolors every hephaestus plot document (`.hep`) it renders with the
brand's semantic colors: `background` becomes the plot's paper,
`foreground` its ink, and `primary` its accent. One of those colors
resolved to a value that is not a hex color, so that one slot was left
as the plot document specifies it. The other slots still apply, and
the warning is raised once per document.

## Why this happens

- **A named CSS color** such as `rebeccapurple` or `navy`. The
  stylesheet side of the brand accepts any CSS color, but a plot is
  laid out outside the browser and only understands hex.
- **A CSS function** such as `rgb(16, 24, 32)` or `hsl(…)`, for the
  same reason.
- **A palette entry that points at one of the above.**

## How to fix

Write the color as `#rgb`, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa` in the brand
file, either directly or in the palette entry the semantic color
refers to.
